items.followUp: What is meant by zero correction of a screw gauge?

rubric.why: Identifies the circular-scale zero’s position for positive zero error.
rubric.how: State that when the screw gauge is closed, the circular-scale zero lies below the reference line.

rubric.why: Identifies the circular-scale zero’s position for negative zero error.
rubric.how: State that when the screw gauge is closed, the circular-scale zero lies above the reference line.

modelAnswer: When the screw gauge is closed, positive zero error occurs if the zero of the circular scale lies below the reference line.
Negative zero error occurs if the zero of the circular scale lies above the reference line.

items.followUp: Name one source of error that can affect a reading on a beam balance.

rubric.why: Recognises that the digital balance gives a direct electronic reading.
rubric.description: States how the digital balance presents the measurement.
rubric.how: Mention that it displays the measured value directly as digits.

rubric.why: Explains that direct digital reading avoids errors involved in reading a beam and pointer.
rubric.how: State that it avoids or reduces reading or parallax errors, making the measurement more accurate.

modelAnswer: A digital electronic balance displays the measured value directly as digits.
This avoids reading and parallax errors that may occur when reading a beam balance, so its measurement is more accurate.
